sections.title: What we built
sections.html: A pipeline that turns one 4K clip of this intersection into traffic-event segments, plus a causal accident-risk curve. It uses a pretrained YOLO11m + ByteTrack for road users, reads the traffic-signal phase from the pixels of the two signal heads that face the camera, uses a scene model of this exact view (crossings, stop line, islands, curb-parking lane, direction zones, and a flow field learned from the samples), and applies eight transparent per-class rules. Measured cold with the official harness, Part A runs at ~0.3× real time and Part A + B at ~1.0× (budget 3×). Everything is open-weights and offline.

sections.title: What worked
items: Reading the lamps. Cutting the signal heads from the full-resolution frame inside the same ffmpeg pass gives a nearly noise-free red/green timeline (< 2 % of samples unreadable). It is the backbone of red_light, stop_line, congestion and the queue exclusions.

Registering every clip to one reference view. The sample framings differ by up to 3 %. Without it the 15-px lamp crops missed the lamps entirely in C3902 (so red_light could never fire there), and every crossing and zone was misplaced. A SIFT + RANSAC homography from a 9-frame median background takes ~5 s and puts all clips within a pixel or two of the reference.
Decoding in ffmpeg. Letting ffmpeg drop frames and resize (with all cores) instead of OpenCV cut Part A from 2.25× to ~0.3× real time.
Perspective-invariant units. Speeds in own-box-heights per second let a single stillness threshold (0.12 h/s) work for a car at the far kerb and one at the bottom edge.

Reviewing every candidate against the footage. Frame strips of each candidate exposed systematic false positives (people walking beside the zebra, cars parked in the curb lane, box jitter at the stop line, amber-phase clearing). Each became a concrete rule change: person-on-road track segments fell from ~270 to 66 once the crossings' walking band was modelled, emitted jaywalking events from 34 to 17, and failure_to_yield from 72 to 37 once only walkers on the painted stripes count.

Risk calibration on normal traffic. Ignoring already-overlapping footprints (occlusion, not danger) and weighting TTC by closing speed pushed the peak hazard on 18 min of normal traffic to ~0.63. In the official harness run the samples raise exactly one alarm: two buses merging side by side through the junction (C3902, 232 s), a genuinely tight interaction but not an accident.

sections.title: What did not work
items: No independent dev set. We reviewed candidates visually but did not produce exhaustive frame-accurate labels for all 18 minutes, so we cannot report F1 or recall with confidence. Missed events (false negatives) are the unknown.

accident and near_miss are not detected in Part A. The samples contain neither, so any rule would be tuned blind, and a false class costs a whole macro-F1 slot. Part B's risk score is our only coverage.
Part B cannot be validated for the same reason: its calibration only guarantees quiet behaviour on normal traffic. mTTA will be short (the alarm fires when footprints are ≲ 0.3 s from contact).

Wrong-way needed tightening. The first version flagged legal turns across the junction box (e.g. a car from the east arm cutting to the south-west). It now only fires against a strongly one-directional lane and is silent on the samples: untested on real positives.

Signal lag. The heads we read run a few seconds ahead of the approach's own lamp (seen only from behind). A 4 s grace period fixes the systematic false red-light runs, but it also hides genuine runs in the first 4 s of red.

Boundary precision. Jaywalking and failure_to_yield segments of overlapping people are unioned (the organisers' convention). On a busy crossing that produces long segments whose IoU with annotations is uncertain.
Dusk clips (C3902, C3905): far pedestrians are detected less reliably, so jaywalking recall on the far carriageway is lower there.

Not attempted: illegal_u_turn / illegal_turn / solid_line_crossing (the legality depends on signage we could not verify), fire_smoke, and debris-type road_obstacle (only animals are detectable with COCO classes).

sections.title: What we would do next
items: Label the four samples exhaustively in CVAT and tune thresholds against evaluate.py at IoU 0.7, especially segment boundaries.
Fine-tune the detector on frames from this camera (pseudo-labels plus corrections), mainly for 15-25 px pedestrians at dusk.
Train a clip classifier (e.g. VideoMAE on DoTA / CCD) to re-score accident and near_miss candidates from the Part B hazard peaks.
Estimate a homography from lane markings to get metric speeds and real TTC, and add lane polylines for solid_line_crossing and illegal turns.
Model the approach's own lamp lag per cycle (from queue discharge) instead of a fixed 4 s grace.
